body: I'm not sure if I am saying something wrong or not, but according to [this](http://book.cakephp.org/3.0/en/orm/database-basics.html#binding-values) you were supposed to use `bindValue()` instead of `bind()` (to keep the arguments the same way that they are, or put brackets on them), and you should also remove the colon from the 1st argument of the functions. In a couple of hours I will try to reproduce the same environment at home and see what I can get to help you. What surprises me is that it works outside the Paginate function.

@sarrala 
Sorry about typing that late... but I only had enough time to test this now...

I noticed this thing that is strange for me... have you created `$this->getAssociations()` ? Because I couldn't find anything closer in the API or Book other than [this](http://api.cakephp.org/3.0/class-Cake.ORM.Association.html) so the use would be something like `$this->Association`, and if you are using CakePHP 2.x there is [this](http://api.cakephp.org/2.6/class-Model.html#_getAssociated) but even though, the proper command is `$this->getAssociated()`.

Maybe in your code is typed in the right way and you mistyped here... or have you copied the code?

@icaroscherma 
`$this->getAssociations()` is just method I use for collecting required associations.
And yes, it belongs to my base controller class and it is not related to cake.
It returns array like this:

``` php
[
    'TableB.TableC',
    'TableX',
]
```

In this case it could as well be:

``` php
$query = $this->Users
    ->find()
    ->contain( ['TableB.TableC'] )
    ->matching('TableB.TableC', function($q) {
        return $q->where(['TableC.time_completed BETWEEN :start AND :end']);
    })
    ->bind(':start', new \DateTime(date('Y-m-01')), 'date')
    ->bind(':end', new \DateTime(date('Y-m-t')), 'date')
    ->distinct(['Users.id']);
```

@sarrala 
Have you tried to change:

```
    ->bind(':start', new \DateTime(date('Y-m-01')), 'date')
    ->bind(':end', new \DateTime(date('Y-m-t')), 'date')
```

to

```
    ->bindValue('start', new \DateTime(date('Y-m-01')), 'date')
    ->bindValue('end', new \DateTime(date('Y-m-t')), 'date')
```

or

```
    ->bind(
        ['start' => new \DateTime(date('Y-m-01')), 'end' => new \DateTime(date('Y-m-t'))],
        ['start' => 'date', 'end' => 'date']
    )
```

Basically changed the `bind()` to `bindValue()` OR use both in arrays, and removed the collons.
But the strange thing is, it's working when Paginate is not used... By the way I'm still checking the Cake files.

@sarrala 

Well, just ignore my previous comment... I tested and without the colon the same error happens even without using the Paginate. The `bindValue` is not working for me (uknown method error) either... I'm looking deeper into the Paginate to see what I can find, seems to be it is missing a proper `bind()` link. And the documentation is missing the colon as you've put in your example and it's the only way that worked for me.

Well, debugging the problem, I found that the problem is in the file `cakephp/src/Controller/Component/PaginatorComponent.php` around line `170`: `$count = $numResults ? $query->count() : 0;`. Seems that the `count()` can`t handle properly the bind values.... I'm checking [this](http://api.cakephp.org/3.0/source-class-Cake.ORM.Query.html#492-527) right now.

~~Edit: Yep, the problem is when the Query is `$complex`, It doesn't get the bind values. (close to line `517`)~~
Edit 2: The `$this` inside the `Query\count()` doesn't get any `params`, and it is supposed to get `:start` and `:end`.
Edit 3: In `PaginatorComponent` close to the line `169` you will have this `$results = $query->all();`, and as soon as `all()` is executed, it will remove the params... but removing this won't fix, so I kept trying to find a way to fix and back again into the `Query\count()` if the query is `$complex`, the execute command is not getting the `$params` (because of the `newQuery()` command), when I debugged it was null.
Sounds like Query::cleanCopy() is losing some state when the query is cloned.

@sarrala @markstory 
Guys, I think I found one solution...

`cakephp/src/Controller/Component/PaginatorComponent.php`

```
line 169
-    $results = $query->all();
+    $results = $query;
```

`cakephp/src/ORM/Query.php`

```
after line 520, add this:
                ->valueBinder($this->valueBinder())

the ELSE should be like:
        {
            $statement = $this->connection()->newQuery()
                ->select($count)
                ->from(['count_source' => $query])
                ->valueBinder($this->valueBinder())
                ->execute();
        }
```

I'm not sure if I'm breaking something with this, but I hope that this helps. I tested with and without using `bind()` and both ways worked for me.
BTW, I'm still testing if I can improve the `PaginatorComponent` code that I changed.

issue.title: Fix bound values being dropped when a clone is made.

repository.name: cakephp
repository.description: CakePHP: The Rapid Development Framework for PHP - Official Repository

issue.body:
Use the clone hook to clear out a query's state. This also moves most of the logic into `__clone`. I'm not sure why I didn't do this earlier, but it makes sense to try and have `clone` be safe.

Refs #6384
